issues.description: PersonResource.createPerson: The solution implementation (PersonResource#createPerson) returns a raw Person and returns null for invalid input, while the NoteResource.createNote endpoint (and the typical pattern in the problem) use ResponseEntity<T> and return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build() on invalid input. Problem statement describes POST /persons should return the saved person in the HTTP response and follows the same REST semantics demonstrated by NoteResource. This discrepancy between returning Person vs ResponseEntity<Person> and returning null vs a ResponseEntity error response is inconsistent and may confuse students about expected HTTP response handling and status codes.
issues.suggestedFix: Change PersonResource#createPerson to return ResponseEntity<Person> and follow the same validation/response pattern as NoteResource: if the incoming Person has a non-null id return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build(); otherwise return ResponseEntity.ok(personService.savePerson(person)). This makes error handling and response types consistent across resources and aligns with the problem description.
